description_full: Phoenix Education Partners, Inc., through its subsidiary, The University of Phoenix, Inc., provides online higher education for working adults in the United States. It develops talent solutions programs for employers, including a talent-sourcing platform that connects employers with students whose skills profiles align with job postings; career services; and degree and non-degree certificate programs. The company was formerly known as AP VIII Queso Holdings, L.P. and changed its name to Phoenix Education Partners, Inc. in September 2025. The company was founded in 1976 and is headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. Phoenix Education Partners, Inc. operates as a subsidiary of Ap Viii Socrates Holdings, L.P.

financial_summary: Phoenix Education Partners, Inc is a small-cap consumer defensive business with a $701M market cap on $1.0B of annual revenue.
Returns on capital run at 174% against a 8% cost of capital — a 167-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $176M in free cash flow — roughly 17 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.21× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 60× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield of 4.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.8% of the shares.
